bib.title: SpanBERT: Improving Pre-training by Representing and Predicting Spans

question: Does pre-training that masks contiguous spans and predicts them from boundary tokens give better span representations than BERT's token masking plus next sentence prediction?
hypothesis: Span selection tasks (QA, coreference) will particularly benefit from span-based pre-training.
contributions: Span masking: mask contiguous random spans (geometric length) instead of random tokens
Span boundary objective (SBO): predict each masked token from the two boundary token encodings plus a relative position embedding
A better-tuned BERT replica baseline; SOTA on OntoNotes coreference, SQuAD 1.1/2.0 results with BERT-large size

method.summary: BERT-large-sized encoder reimplemented in fairseq and pre-trained on BooksCorpus plus English Wikipedia with geometric span masking (15% of tokens), MLM plus SBO loss, single 512-token segments and no NSP. Compared with Google BERT, a tuned BERT reimplementation and a single-sequence BERT, then fine-tuned on QA, coreference, TACRED and GLUE.
method.task: masked-language-model pre-training with span objectives, then fine-tuning

datasets.name: BooksCorpus + English Wikipedia
datasets.source: same corpus as BERT; cased WordPiece tokens
datasets.preprocessing: corpus divided into single contiguous blocks of up to 512 tokens (to document boundary); different masks each epoch

datasets.name: SQuAD 1.1 / 2.0
datasets.preprocessing: SQuAD 2.0 unanswerable: answer span set to [CLS]

datasets.name: MRQA: NewsQA, TriviaQA, SearchQA, HotpotQA, Natural Questions
datasets.split: MRQA dev set split in half into new dev and test
datasets.preprocessing: MRQA contexts truncated to 800 tokens, only answerable questions kept

datasets.name: GLUE (8 tasks; WNLI excluded, set to majority class 65.1%)

other.SBO head: 2-layer FFN, GeLU, LayerNorm; input [x_{s-1}; x_{e+1}; p_{i-s+1}]
other.embedding tying: input embedding reused for target tokens in MLM and SBO

models.name: Our BERT
models.architecture: BERT-large reimplementation with improved preprocessing and optimisation

models.name: Our BERT-1seq
models.architecture: Our BERT trained on single full-length sequences without NSP

training.objective: L(x_i) = L_MLM(x_i) + L_SBO(x_i), summed over tokens in masked spans; no NSP
training.optimizer: AdamW (decoupled weight decay), beta1=0.9, beta2=0.999, epsilon 1e-8
training.batch_size: 256 sequences of up to 512 tokens (about 390 sequences on average)
training.dropout: 0.1 on all layers and attention weights

other.masking: 15% of tokens masked; span lengths ~ Geo(p=0.2) clipped at 10 words, mean 3.8; complete words; start uniform at word start; 80/10/10 [MASK]/random/original applied per span
other.fine-tuning QA: max_seq_length 512, sliding window 128, lr {5e-6,1e-5,2e-5,3e-5,5e-5}, batch {16,32}, 4 epochs
other.fine-tuning coref: max_seq_length {128,256,384,512}, BERT lr {1e-5,2e-5}, task lr {1e-4,2e-4,3e-4}, 20 epochs, batch 1 document
other.fine-tuning TACRED/GLUE: max_seq_length 128, lr as QA, batch {16,32}, 10 epochs (CoLA 4)

metrics.name: F1 / EM
metrics.definition: SQuAD and MRQA span overlap F1 and exact match

metrics.name: Coreference average F1
metrics.definition: mean F1 of MUC, B3 and CEAF-phi4

metrics.name: GLUE
metrics.definition: per-task metrics, average includes WNLI at majority class

eval.protocol: Single reported numbers per cell; fine-tuning hyperparameters chosen from grids; seeds, variance and significance tests not reported. Ablations use dev sets and 1.2M-step checkpoints.

availability.weights: pre-trained models released at same URL

limits: Single runs, no seeds or significance tests reported; fine-tuning hyperparameters tuned from grids per task.
Ablations use 1.2M-step checkpoints and dev sets, so not directly comparable to main results.
The NSP explanation is a hypothesis (longer context or noise from unrelated documents), not isolated by experiment.
Only BERT-large size and BooksCorpus+Wikipedia; no scaling study. Authors say XLNet and RoBERTa are concurrent and use more data/tuning.
Random subword masking was better on coreference without SBO.
Dated: encoder-only MLM pre-training; later work scaled data and dropped these objectives.

terms.definition: predicting each token of a masked span using only the representations of the observed tokens at the boundaries
